clue.text: Turn meat over with some wood

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the first two words are read backwards

blocks.note: a turn in a game is a go
ham is a cured meat
'some' and 'any' are interchangeable in questions: have you any?

explanation.surface: A cook flips a joint of meat on a wooden board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' applies to the first two words together, not just to meat, and the turned pair comes before 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown tropical timber, a specific example of the general category named.

clue.text: Large amount rolled inside of fine fabric

indicators.note: something rolled over turns end to end, so the first pieces read upwards in this down entry

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a sum is an amount of money
inside means in

explanation.surface: A huge bolt of delicate cloth is rolled up at a draper's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large amount' is the reversed part: L SUM rolled gives MUSL, and IN finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslin is a lightweight, loosely woven cotton cloth, used for dresses and straining food.

clue.text: Early advantage of promotion above street in centre

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for centre

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, promotes a product
St is the address abbreviation for street
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: Someone gets an early boost from a promotion to an office above a central street.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'above' simply means placed before, so the promotion comes ahead of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is a lead given or gained at the beginning of a race or competition.

clue.text: Young wife precooked wild bird

indicators.note: wild suggests something running out of control, so the letters of the cooking word are rearranged

blocks.note: green means inexperienced or young
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
the nine letters of precooked rearranged

explanation.surface: A young wife serves a ready-cooked game bird for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild bird' reads as a game dish, but 'wild' is the anagram signal and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The green woodpecker is a large British woodland species with green plumage and a red crown.

clue.text: Attention held by shelter easiest to reach?

indicators.note: held by means enclosed by, so the word for attention sits inside the word for shelter

blocks.note: to lend an ear is to pay attention
a nest is a bird's shelter

explanation.surface: A shelter that catches attention is described as the most accessible one.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a loose paraphrase: the closest thing is the easiest to get to.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest place is the one requiring the least travel, so it is the simplest to get to.

clue.text: Curve on map is essentially ignored by local

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub ignores a curved line drawn on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the nearby pub, here shortened to BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather chart joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Flag pests around beach rubbish on top of shingle

the opening letter of shingle

clue.text: Loyal voters left European city

blocks.note: a party's base is its core of loyal supporters
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb meaning departed, but it simply supplies L.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine, close to the borders with France and Germany.

explanation.definitionFit: Something that radiates spreads outward from a centre, like spokes from a hub.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like a race, but it is the noun for keeping something going.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost and work of maintaining something, as in the running costs of a house.

clue.text: Had food on back of empty steel pan

indicators.note: an emptied word loses everything inside, so only its outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of steel
had food means ate

explanation.surface: Someone ate food from the back of an empty steel pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' is the kitchen item in the surface but a verb, to criticise harshly, in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play or film is to criticise it severely, just as a critic might pan it.

clue.text: Spare iPad somehow given a value

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Appraised means assessed for worth, as when an expert estimates the price of an item.

clue.text: Lying at home after Sunday school class?

blocks.note: someone at home is in
since means after, as in 'since the war'
RE is Religious Education, the sort of lesson taught at Sunday school

explanation.surface: A child skips Sunday school and stays at home, and lies about it.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for Religious Education, a school subject in Britain; the question mark admits Sunday school is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying and insincere both describe someone saying things they do not truly mean or believe.

clue.text: Charlie recalled hosting naked gala dance

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word for Charlie is read backwards

blocks.note: a charlie is a fool, an ass; the word is reversed
gala without its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a charlie is a fool, an ass; reversed it wraps around AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance that grew out of Cuban son and mambo rhythms.

clue.text: Victor interrupting frisky actor’s frolic

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the five letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Card game oddly calmer after a lot of wine

oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters only: first, third, fifth

blocks.note: Pinot is a grape and the wine made from it
the first, third and fifth letters of calmer

explanation.surface: A card player grows strangely calmer after drinking a great deal of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the wine first, even though it comes second in the clue.

the BMA, British Medical Association, is the doctors' body; reversed
a ridge is a long raised bank of earth

explanation.walkthrough: The BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city in East Anglia, standing on the River Cam.

clue.text: Friendly novelist abridged message

blocks.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists
a cable is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A friendly writer sends a shortened message.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin are the crossword's favourite novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means showing goodwill and getting on well, without quarrelling or hostility.

clue.text: Ring performer Mike visiting a party with Republican

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
visiting a place means being at it
taken as written
a do is a party
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A circus act called Mike drops in on a party with a Republican friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring performer' suggests a circus or boxing; the ring is the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, performing in the arena of a bullring.

clue.text: Queen greeting Poles housing old animals

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the last pair of letters goes around another

blocks.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
hi is a greeting
N and S, the north and south poles
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: The Queen greets some Polish people living in old housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinos are large thick-skinned horned mammals of Africa and Asia, a particular kind of beast.

clue.text: Advises American screening seed supplier

indicators.note: screening means concealing, so the answer lies hidden across the words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A consultant advises an American who is vetting a seed company.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside adviSES AMErican.
explanation.definitionFit: The sesame plant produces small oily seeds used in baking and for oil, so it supplies them.

clue.text: Triumphal expression of drunk with present

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
someone present is here

explanation.surface: A drunk exclaims in triumph upon receiving a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: So there is a defiant exclamation said when you think you have won an argument.

clue.text: Romeo takes off for cheeky run across pitch?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged with the R

explanation.surface: A lover strips off and dashes across a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' reads as undressing, apt for the definition, but 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, famously at sports matches.

clue.text: Adult and child inspired by church store

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to be breathed in, so the first two pieces go inside the church

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
ch is the abbreviation for child
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A grown-up and a child are moved by a visit to a church shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden supply or stockpile of goods, kept for later use.

clue.text: Colonel eviscerated reptile in hold

indicators.note: an eviscerated thing has had its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Colonel
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A colonel guts a snake held in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp is to grip or hold something tightly in the hand or arms.

clue.text: Read Pinter after cycling on front of tandem

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so the playwright's first letter moves to the end
the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Harold Pinter, the playwright, with his first letter cycled to the back
re means on or concerning
the opening letter of tandem

explanation.surface: Someone reads Pinter's play while out riding a tandem bicycle.

explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation or text in a particular way is to interpret it, giving it a meaning.

clue.text: Liberal blocking second delivery of total budget shortfall?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second delivery' looks like a cricket ball; 'second' is the verb, and 'delivery' marks spoken sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A black hole in public finances is a large unexplained gap where money has vanished.

clue.text: Father quietly covering chapter in trained group

explanation.definitionFit: A business empire is a large group of companies under single ownership or control.

clue.text: Modern offices secured finally by river for media centre

the closing letters of offices and of secured
